## Part B -- Subsetting (Accessing) Vectors
```{r}
grades <- c(88, 92, 79, 95, 84)
names(grades) <- c("Math", "Science", "English", "History", "PE")
grades[3]
grades[c(1,4)]
grades[c("Science","PE")]
```
```{r}
grades[-c(1,4) ]
```
```{r}
grades[grades >= 85]
```

## Part C -- Vector Operations and append()
```{r}

y <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)
result <- x+y
result
x*2
```
```{r}
z <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
short <- c(1,0)
z + short
```
```{r}
fruits <- c("apple", "banana", "cherry")
append(fruits, "date")
append(fruits, "kiwi", after = 1)
```

## Part D -- Lists: Creating and Subsetting
```{r}
student <- list(name = "Maria Santos", age = 20, grades = c(88, 92, 79), is_enrolled = TRUE)
```

```{r}
student["grades"]
class(student["grades"])
```
```{r}
student$name
```
```{r}
student[["grades"]][2]
student$grades[2]
```
##Question #10
##student["grades"] will write the entire elements on that length. while the [["grades"]] will only select a specific element.

## Part E--Critical Thinking Challenge
```{r}
inventory <- list(item = c("Notebook", "Pen", "Eraser"), price = c(24.50, 10.00, 5.00), in_stock = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
print(inventory$item [inventory$in_stock==TRUE])
```
```{r}
inventory$item <- append(inventory$item, "Ruler")
inventory$price <- append(inventory$price, 15.00)
inventory$in_stock <- append(inventory$in_stock, TRUE)
```
##Question #12

##"inventory$in_stock" extracts the logical vector c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE). While the "inventory$item" extracts the character vector c("Notebook","Pen","Eraser").Both vectors have the same length and the "[]" with the logical vector keeps the elements where the value is TRUE.

## Conclusion
##Vectors hold many values of a single type, ehile it lists can holf elements of different types and lengths, including other vectors and lists. Vectors use [] for indexing, while lists use [] to get smaller list and [[]] or $ is to extract the element itself.
